title: Centralized Billing Request Funnel and Prioritization Heuristics for Commitments & Marketplace
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Establish a repeatable, centralized intake funnel and concise prioritization heuristics for non-bug billing requests (commitments, invoicing exceptions, marketplace allocations). The goal is to reduce time-to-decision, align outcomes with commercial risk and revenue impact, and minimize ad-hoc email/Slack escalation overhead.
problem_statement: We receive a high volume of billing and packaging questions via multiple channels (sales, support, partners, finance) with inconsistent documentation. Decisions are currently ad-hoc, leading to revenue leakage, missed invoices, and uneven customer experiences for commitment/marketplace deals.
goals: Create a single intake form + routing rules that captures commercial context and required artifacts.
Define a lightweight prioritization rubric that balances revenue risk, legal/compliance constraints, and engineering effort.
Set SLA targets for first acknowledgment and final decision for each priority tier.
Provide templates and decision logs so outcomes are reproducible and auditable for finance and legal teams.
out_of_scope: Billing SE technical bugs, routine invoice payment failures, or post-contract disputes that require legal ops. Those are handled by Support/Legal and not through this triage funnel.
intake_flow_steps: 1) Customer-facing team (AE/CS/Partner PD) submits standardized Billing Intake form (Confluence + form link) with required artifacts: SOW/commitment, invoice, marketplace listing, suggested remedy.
2) Automated pre-check validates required fields and assigns a triage score (revenue impact estimate, timeframe, regulatory constraints).
3) Triage coordinator (role: Billing PM) reviews pre-check within SLA and assigns Priority Tier (P0/P1/P2).
4) If P0/P1, schedule 30-minute decision sync with Finance + Legal + Solutions within 48 hours; if P2, queue for weekly backlog review.
5) Record decision, rationale, and owner in Decision Log and notify requester with next steps and estimated timeline.
prioritization_criteria: Revenue at risk: >$50k ARR or one-time revenue >$25k -> higher priority.
Customer tier: Enterprise customers with active Dedicated/Private deployments escalate one level.
Legal/compliance constraints: If request touches data residency, auditability, or contract clauses, escalate regardless of dollar value.
Marketplace complexity: requests that require marketplace billing code changes or partner revenue-sharing are higher effort and are triaged by the Marketplace squad.
Operational risk: high frequency issues (repeat invoices, systemic allocation errors) increase priority.
decision_rubric: Accept: Implement configuration/credit/one-off invoice adjustment under standard playbook; document in Decision Log and close.
Conditional Accept: Approve with guardrails (time-limited credits, revised contract milestone) and require follow-up engineering/ops story.
Reject: Clear rationale (policy, unsupported request) and offer alternative path (billing credit, product workaround).
Escalate to Legal: Any contract amendment or unusual credit >$250k or changes that alter revenue recognition.
Escalate to Exec Review: Strategic accounts where the request materially affects renewal or deal closure.
roles_and_responsibilities: Billing PM (Triage Coordinator): owns intake form, SLA adherence, decision logs, and routing.
Finance: validates revenue impact, approves invoice adjustments, and updates recognition guidance.
Legal: reviews contract changes and signs off on exceptions that affect terms.
Marketplace Product Manager: evaluates marketplace allocation, partner flows, and operational effort.
Engineering (Billing/Backend): estimates implementation effort for system-side changes and provides ETA.
Customer Success / AE: provides business context, proposed remedies, and customer acceptance criteria.
escalation_paths: Standard escalation: Triage Coordinator -> Finance Lead -> Legal Counsel; target escalation time 48 hours for P0/P1.
Executive escalation: If decision would likely delay renewal >30 days or change contract economics materially, escalate to Head of Revenue and Head of Product within 24 hours.
Operational incident: If the triage uncovers systemic billing failure, create incident ENG-INCxxx and trigger Reliability runbook.
required_artifacts_and_templates: Billing Intake Form (Google Form): captures SOW, invoice number, customer tier, suggested remedy, and commercial owner.
Decision Log Template (Confluence): fields for ID, date, requester, decision, rationale, owner, and follow-up stories.
Invoice Adjustment Template (Finance Sheet): standardized credit workflow to reduce reconciliation errors.
Marketplace Allocation Change Request (Doc): checklist for partner revenue, tax treatment, and SKU mapping.
metrics_and_SLAs: Acknowledgement SLA: P0/P1 within 24 hours, P2 within 72 hours.
Decision SLA: P0 within 72 hours, P1 within 7 business days, P2 in next triage cycle (14 days).
Success metrics: reduction in time-to-decision, % of requests resolved without executive review, and decreased invoice disputes month-over-month.
Operational metric: number of post-decision chargebacks or corrections (target <1% of adjusted invoices).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Build intake form, Decision Log, and run pilot with Revenue Ops and 5 AE teams.
Phase 2 (4 weeks): Iterate on prioritization thresholds based on pilot data; integrate automated pre-checks for required artifacts.
Phase 3 (6 weeks): Expand to Support, Marketplace partners, and publish public-facing guideline for customers and partners.
Phase 4: Automate routing into Jira/Linear and add dashboards to Console for volume & SLA tracking.
open_questions: What is the exact revenue threshold for automatic P0 escalation (proposal: $50k ARR)?
Do we allow AEs to grant ad-hoc credits under a delegated authority and what limits should apply?
How should marketplace partner revenue-sharing changes be reflected in billing vs. partner payouts?
What level of audit trail is required by Finance for compliance in EMEA vs. US?
